name: The Frazer household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: fraser_wm_h

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-01-28, 27 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-01-28 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

name_ruling.takes: the reading T-0424 made at the page image of the ninth impression, which sets 'Wm. H. Frazer'
name_ruling.over: the reading chicago_democrat_1834_01_28#c001 made from a transcription, which set 'Wm. H. Fraser' and was normalized to 'Wm. H. Fraser'
name_ruling.reasoning: Both readings set plain, complete letters and they disagree — two impressions of one return, re-keyed by the compositor. The roster is `scan_verified` and the transcription `transcription_mediated`, and tools/read_letter_list_1834_image.py already rules that the image OVERTURNS an uncut transcription reading the printed line contradicts. Nothing outside this return carries the overturned letters.
name_ruling.the_id_did_not_move: person_id 'fraser_wm_h' and household 'hh_fraser_wm_h' are cited by the crosswalks, identity_master.json, the smoke cohorts and card_merge_rulings.json. An id is a handle, not a claim, so the displayed name moves and the id stands (T-1139 rule N5).

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Wm. H. Fraser' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 28 January 1834, column 1 — dated 1834-01-28. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: Wm. H. Fraser and Wm. H. Frazer are separate stable postal IDs in the same cohort only weeks apart in early 1834. The one-letter surname variation is a strong duplicate/transcription lead, but no external identity discriminator was found.

candidates.basis: Near-identical full initials/name and closely spaced 1834 postal dates.
conflicts: No independent source yet resolves whether one or two people.

merged_from.note: THE UNION OF THE CARDS THIS PERSON WAS SPLIT ACROSS. The sources and evidence blocks above include everything the folded cards cited; each folded record is kept whole under data/residents/merged/ and is redirected by index.json's `merged` table. The reasoning for the merge is in data/residents/card_merge_rulings.json.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
